promptCards.title: Seed Drawer Map Details
promptCards.teacherSetup: Place three seed packets or blank index cards at the writing table and ask students to point to one map-room detail before they write.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Describe the seed library map room so a classmate can picture where the hidden garden note belongs.
writingLines: The first place I notice in the map room is ____________________
A tiny object on the table looks like ____________________
The map clue is tucked beside ____________________
My setting helps the story because ____________________
promptCards.shareMove: Ask partners to trade papers and underline one detail they can picture clearly.
promptCards.extension: Students add a small map label in the margin and write one sentence explaining it.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The student includes at least three concrete setting details tied to the story task.

promptCards.title: Solar Oven Picnic Fix
promptCards.teacherSetup: Draw a quick three-step test chart on the board with problem, try, and result columns.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Help the picnic team choose a fair fix when one solar oven warms a snack faster than the others.
writingLines: The picnic station problem is ____________________
My hero tries this first fix: ____________________
The result shows ____________________
The fair solution for the team is ____________________
promptCards.shareMove: Have students read only their solution sentence to a table partner.
promptCards.extension: Students sketch a before-and-after test card with one label for each change.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The student names a clear problem and connects the solution to evidence from the scene.

promptCards.title: Moss Observatory Senses
promptCards.teacherSetup: Invite students to list quiet forest words for sight, touch, sound, and smell before drafting.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Write a calm observatory scene where moss details help your hero understand a nature message.
writingLines: The observatory air feels ____________________
A quiet sound nearby is ____________________
The sensory clue tells my hero ____________________
promptCards.shareMove: Invite volunteers to share one sensory word, not the whole paragraph.
promptCards.extension: Students revise one plain word into a more exact sensory word.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The student uses sensory details that make the observatory scene more specific.

promptCards.title: Spoon Ferry Dock Dialogue
promptCards.teacherSetup: Model one polite question and one helpful answer on the board before students write their own lines.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Write a short dockside conversation that helps the spoon ferry deliver the right lunchbox order.
writingLines: The ferry cook asks this question: ____________________
The dock helper answers with: ____________________
My hero says this polite line: ____________________
The conversation solves ____________________
promptCards.shareMove: Partners read the three spoken lines in quiet voices and check whether the order makes sense.
promptCards.extension: Students add one action tag that shows who is speaking without using a name.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The student writes dialogue that sounds polite and moves the scene forward.

promptCards.title: Museum Label Choice
promptCards.teacherSetup: Show students how a museum curator chooses one clue to place first and one clue to save for later.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Decide which exhibit label your curator should write first so visitors notice the best clue.
writingLines: My curator chooses the exhibit called ____________________
The label should mention ____________________
The curator waits to reveal ____________________
This choice helps visitors because ____________________
promptCards.shareMove: Students hold up one finger for first, second, or third clue choice before discussing with a partner.
promptCards.extension: Students write a second version of the label for younger museum visitors.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The student explains a character choice with a reason connected to the visitor experience.

promptCards.title: Compass Craft Route Order
promptCards.teacherSetup: Give students three sticky notes or paper scraps so they can physically order the route before writing.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Plan the order of stops for a craft-academy map route that leads to a finished story project.
writingLines: First, my map route goes to ____________________
Next, the compass points toward ____________________
After that, my hero checks ____________________
The final stop is important because ____________________
promptCards.shareMove: Students compare only their first and final stops with a nearby writer.
promptCards.extension: Students add transition words above each line and read the route again.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The student uses ordered steps that make the route easy to follow.

promptCards.title: Almost Invention Sentence Test
promptCards.teacherSetup: Write a short sentence, a longer because sentence, and a question sentence on the board as examples.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Test an almost-invention by writing sentences that do not all start or sound the same.
writingLines: My short sentence: ____________________
My because sentence: ____________________
My question sentence: ____________________
My best invention sentence is ____________________
promptCards.shareMove: Ask students to star the sentence type they used least and share that one with a partner.
promptCards.extension: Students combine two short sentences into one smoother sentence.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The student tries at least three sentence patterns while staying on the same invention idea.

promptCards.title: Binding Day Ending Choice
promptCards.teacherSetup: Ask students to choose whether their booklet ending should feel helpful, funny, or thoughtful before they write.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Write an ending for Binding Day that shows how the finished booklet is shared in the classroom.
writingLines: At the boardwalk table, the finished booklet shows ____________________
My hero chooses to end with ____________________
The class notices ____________________
The final sentence of my story is ____________________
promptCards.shareMove: Students read their final sentence only and let partners name the ending feeling.
promptCards.extension: Students draft a second ending with a different feeling and circle the stronger one.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The student writes an ending that matches the story action and leaves a clear final feeling.

promptCards.title: Index Card Theater Table Share
promptCards.teacherSetup: Arrange students in pairs and give each writer one index card for a scene title or favorite line.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Prepare a tiny theater-club share that lets a partner understand your scene without reading the whole story.
writingLines: My scene is called ____________________
One line I can share is ____________________
One prop or action that helps is ____________________
A kind question for my partner is ____________________
promptCards.shareMove: Partners share one card each, then say one thing they understood clearly.
promptCards.extension: Students add a tiny cue mark where a reader should pause.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The student selects a short shareable piece and responds to a peer with a kind question or comment.

promptCards.title: Revision River Two-Pass
promptCards.teacherSetup: Tell students to pick one sentence from yesterday or from a quick draft and copy it onto the first line.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Ride the revision ferry by changing one sentence so it becomes clearer and more interesting.
writingLines: My first sentence is ____________________
The revision move I chose is ____________________
My revised sentence is ____________________
The revised version is clearer because ____________________
promptCards.shareMove: Students point to the changed word or phrase instead of reading the whole draft aloud.
promptCards.extension: Students make one more small revision and label it with the move they used.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The student makes a visible revision and can explain how the change improves the sentence.
